K-54 says in that period that civilian trucks were requisitioned and that a civilian truck was taken and things from richer houses as well and that an officer took all of that to Serbia. I'm interested in the following. On that occasion, in that area, were motor vehicles requisitioned, trucks too, and were such acts committed as described by this witness?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, this is 1998. Absolutely not a single vehicle, because there was no need for that, had been mobilised for the Army of Yugoslavia. We had our own vehicles. As for this kind of a case occurring in my unit without me knowing it, in view of the functioning of the chain of command and in view of the functioning of the security line, that is absolutely impossible. That witness is not telling the truth in that specific case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Had something like that had happened, what would you have done?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that officer would have been arrested at the same instant and he would have been sent to military court with criminal charges brought against him. I never needed officers like that. I did have one such incident there committed by a sergeant, but he was arrested and he was sent further on to a regular military court with criminal charges brought against him in Nis. This is Sergeant Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. The same witness, K-54, asserts that in the summer of 1998, in the month of August, at a place that's about 15 kilometres away from Djakovica, he pointed out that you were next to a tank and that he was about 10 metres away from you and that he could hear you order firing at a civilian house. Is his assertion correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will redact from page 47 -- in fact -- yes, 47, line 18, until now, and leave it to you to try to avoid any further indication of the identity of the witness. Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I'm now going to ask you about a place called Ljubizda Has and February 1999. We have heard a claim that the bodies of six Albanians had been brought there from the direction of a mountain where ambushes were laid. Do you know anything about that? Could you explain briefly?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well about that because I was there, but that is not true. It was not six bodies, it was three bodies that were brought, the bodies of terrorists who were killed while in ambush by our forces that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were any weaponry and equipment seized?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A large amount of equipment was seized. It was our assessment that based on that amount of equipment that group could have counted 50 members and they ran into a seven-man ambush on our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where was the ambush?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Mount Pastrik. A kilometre and a half to 2 kilometres away overlooking Ljubizda village, Ljubizda Has village in the mountains. In my reports you can probably find the exact location, but I know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 2 kilometres away from what?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Ljubizda Has village, but towards the Albanian border and in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is that in the border belt?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's all in the border belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number 3D1051, please. Count 2.4, please. In English that is on second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we have before us a document from the 3rd Army command, security section. In paragraph 2.4, we see that in Jeskovo village a DTG, sabotage terrorist group, was stationed numbering 25 persons, Jeskovo village. Did you get this information?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had this information and we had our own intelligence. It was in the beginning of March that we knew that in the vicinity of Prizren in Kabas and in Jeskovo new groups of terrorists had arrived for the purpose of mobilising new forces and with the objective of attacking Prizren-Zur Dragas road and on the other side, Prizren-Suva Reka road in the area of Korisa village.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you look at paragraph 2.5. In B/C/S it's page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S, this is on second page, please. Could we have that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this paragraph, there is a reference to Kabas village. Is that the one you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the same report I notified the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What steps did you take next?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I notified the corps commander that there was a danger that in addition to large terrorist forces located in Retimlje village, Gorane village, Ram Dubrava, Studencane villages, that these forces after carrying out a mobilisation could practically encircle Prizren and cut off my communications, my roads that lead from Prizren to the road so that I wouldn't be able to supply my units any longer. And on the other side they could cut off the roads that go from Metohija towards Suva Reka and Dulje leading to Kosovo Polje, towards Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have on our screens Exhibit Number P2067.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your order, the one you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After those telegrams sent to the corps command containing proposals and after their approval, this is the order I issued to engage units, to destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the broader area of Jeskovo village, dated 9 March.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In this operation did you have any coordinated action with MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this operation we had the coordinated support of the local MUP from Prizren and the forces of the 37th Detachment of PJP, in fact, the 5th Company of PJP from Prizren and the 37th Detachment of PJP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Give me a moment, please, Mr. Cepic. Sorry, Mr. Cepic, that had to be dealt with just now. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, the forces of the police that you enumerated, did you have any effective control over them?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could not have any control over police forces because they had their own commander, with whom I had agreed coordination, but throughout the time he commanded his own units just like I commanded the parts of my brigade that were involved. We were located in the same place, and in my view that was a desirable practice that I always followed whenever we had coordinated action with the MUP because that's the easier way to organize coordination so that I can assist MUP forces when they need me and they can assist me when I need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have second page and count 5, 5.6 and 5.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we see here is an enumeration of those forces, the 37th PJP Detachment and the 5th Company of PJP Prizren in -- under the heading: "Tasks to units." Why did you refer to these two units specifically?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, in this specific assignment, my forces do not go behind MUP forces supporting them. Instead, since there were not enough forces they take up positions on the blockade line together, next to MUP forces, so that each of my commanders who had received their respective assignments, especially those who were neighbours to the MUP, had to know exactly what the MUP's tasks were. You don't have my combat assets following MUP forces and supporting them. They were in the same location, and myself and the commander of the 37th Detachment were in one place. And whenever some sort of support was needed, I dealt with it on his request. My units established - let me say - control or visual control and coordinated action with the MUP directly on the lines, and they moved practically in one line of blockade, shoulder to shoulder. And since the map, the decision map, usually doesn't reach my commanders, they only get the order, each one of them has to know not only their own task but the task of their left neighbour and their right neighbour, in order to avoid any possibility of friendly fire, to avoid the possibility that somebody intrude into another person's axis, suffering losses. We had to regulate and define very precisely the task for each of my units, and the tasks of the MUP units were agreed during the coordination efforts. So the MUP units knew exactly how my units were moving and when and where they were allowed to open fire or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were there any civilians in that village?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in Jeskovo there were no civilians, not a single one of them; there were only terrorists inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we already have in e-court system admitted Exhibit 5D112, this is the report from OSCE mission, paragraph 4, and in that paragraph there is a sentence: When the mission underlined that that village was abandoned. If it's necessary, we can show that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, General, was that terrorist practice of two villages, one housing terrorists, another civilians, used in this case?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could say so because in front of that village there are Bilusa village, Hoca Zagradska village, on the same line exactly, and Leskovec village. In those villages, the complete population was there, whereas in Jeskovo there was not a single resident. And as soon as the army appeared, it had to go through Hoca Zagradska village. And even before the army arrived, while we were still on the asphalt road, that village organized itself and the inhabitants moved towards Prizren; however, they were stopped while they were still close to the village. They were stopped by the MUP, and they were told that there was absolutely no need for them to leave their village. They stayed for a while then, until the units passed through towards the blockade line, and later the request was made for all of them to return to their homes and they did because neither they nor their village were affected by the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have on our screens Exhibit Number P1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your document?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is my document which I sent to the command of the Pristina Corps on the very next day after the activities were carried out. It's an analysis of the activities of my forces when routing the Siptar terrorist forces in the village of Jeskovo, and of course I delivered it according to the order of the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We have heard here in this courtroom that you ordered, in the course of that action, that anyone found there should be killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say right away that that is not correct. It doesn't make sense. I cannot imagine a single professional officer anywhere in the world, not just our army, who could issue such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me at that point in time, when this action was being carried out, where was the rear battalion?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rear battalion was not a combat unit. It had its task only in blocking an axis along which we did not expect any fighting or any pull-out by the terrorist forces, and that was the asphalt road going from the village of Zur toward the Dragas plateau and Dragas. In that area, these units were located which were not combat units, part of the logistics battalion and some other forces which were not intended for combat action but --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What is the distance? How far was this away?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the asphalt road is about a kilometre or a kilometre and a half away from the village of Jeskovo and from the village of Bilusa also and about 2 kilometres from the village of Zagradska, that's just a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the bottom of the page, please. In B/C/S -- could we have the bottom of the page in B/C/S and, thank you, and in English it's probably on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2, paragraph 3, you say: "The forces that were engaged in the execution of the task had been carefully planned and the coordination within the forces and cooperation with the MUP forces were excellent." Can you please explain what this means.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means that the forces and means for this task had been carefully planned, which is why it was executed successfully. And it's quite normal that the army forces and the MUP forces should cooperate in this task and engage in coordinated action because they were organs of the same state. So it was to be expected that they would cooperate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the second page in B/C/S and in English is probably the bottom page -- page 3 in English probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at the middle of the page, the fourth paragraph in Serbian, it says: Command of the selected forces ... Would you read that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Command of the selected forces was unified through a joint command of the MUP and VJ forces; it was safe and timely."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what it says here?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, almost in all the actions I had with the MUP, the MUP commander and I would be together at one location. When the conditions were unfavourable, as in this case, I was with the deputy commander at one place and my deputy would be at another point with the MUP commander. And that was what I call a combined command post. We would be there together, monitor the fighting together, agree on coordination and joint action on the spot. He would pass on orders to his units and I would pass on orders to mine. Any requests that the MUP commander komandir sent to their commander, for support or some kind of assistance, he would pass on that information to me on the spot, and then I would implement it with the resources I have for support or through my officers. And likewise, if I needed assistance somewhere, that was the simplest thing. My junior commanders would tell me and then I would directly inform the MUP commander standing next to me about the problem and what kind of assistance I needed. And this functioned quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The translation of that answer is very confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Whether that's the answer or the translation isn't clear. I'll have the answer retranslated later from the B/C/S tape to clarify the position, but, Mr. Cepic, you need to make it clear to us where the two commanders were and where the deputies were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you said in your previous reply that you and a MUP representative would be on one location and your deputy and another representative of the MUP would be in another location. Could you give us a specific example of where this was and how this functioned.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would need to see a map. I was to the south-east of the village of Jeskovo, about a kilometre away, on a hill overlooking the village of Jeskovo, quite a lot higher than it, and the commander was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't need the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who was in what you described as the joint command post? And I think you've now answered that. You say you were with the commander of the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I and the MUP commander and the auxiliary organs, my communications man, my driver, the MUP commander's driver, my security and his security, that would be between five and ten men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And where was your deputy and the deputy commander of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said in principle -- well, in this particular situation they did not have any roles to play. In certain other situations when the territory was far larger, then on one axis I would go there with the deputy MUP commander and the MUP commander with my deputy would go to the other axis. But in this particular case it was only the two of us and only the two of us were in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who did you cooperate with most frequently from the MUP? Can we clarify this issue, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the territory of Prizren municipality there is a secretariat of the interior in Prizren which had its OUPs in Orahovac, Suva Reka, and Dragas, and I cooperated usually with the chief of the secretariat. In 1998 that was Colonel Zekavica. In 1999 that was Colonel Milos Vojinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were my counterparts, more or less. When we were carrying out coordination, the commander of the 37th Detachment, Colonel Mitrovic, would be called to the secretariat in Prizren and in the secretariat we would meet. On the maps we would specify how both sets of forces were to act.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, the terrorists who were killed in Jeskovo, what sort of uniforms did they have?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the terrorists killed in Jeskovo wore black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we already have in e-court system admitted Exhibits 5D113 and 5D114, also reports from OSCE mission and it is described in those reports about that event and about black uniforms. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, was there confirmation from the KLA that their members were killed there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, much later, after the war, reading a book written by the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 125th Brigade was called Xhafer Berisha. I learned because he described these events also and I found it interesting because it was in my zone and because he was describing the same battles in which I participated, and it was then that I learned the names of those nine members of the special unit from the 125th Brigade. And as he says, these were heroes killed in fighting with the Serb forces at close range, 15 to 20 metres, and he lists their nine names.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You don't have to tell me their names. I'm interested what KLA brigade was in question.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 125th KLA Brigade from the Pastrik zone and its commander was Ekrem Rexha, also known as Drini; and the 125th Brigade covered part of the territory of Prizren municipality, which is called Vrini.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, we'll now move on to another location, to Trnje, late March. We have heard some testimony by members of the rear battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So first -- [In English] P1981, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This document is under seal, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we go to private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will be asking questions that mean that we need to hear about the content, will you, because we can simply just not show it on the screens outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's try that first of all, but if you need to go into private session to ask a question then we'll do that. Mr. Delic, if you can answer the questions without going into the detail reflected in the document, that would help; otherwise, if you find it difficult, let me know and we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, certainly I can. These are documents which were used in 2005, and there was never a private session. I can answer in every case without these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, I'm only interested in one thing. We don't have to go through the document. It's an order issued by you, but I'm only interested in the rear battalion. Is that a manoeuvre component? Is that unit in a blockade? Does it have a third task? Can you explain about the rear battalion.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rear battalion is a logistical unit for supplies. It's not a combat unit, it's not a manoeuvre unit, it doesn't receive combat tasks except to protect itself in the areas where it's located. In this particular case, as this was a large area of land which had to be blocked, they received the task on one axis where it was not expected or there was a very small likelihood that various forces would turn up. They were to be there and seal off a certain territory together with other non-combat units, such as the communications company, the engineers company. They were to seal off that territory which was some seven, eight, or ten kilometres long, and through that line of blockade to prevent terrorist forces from pulling out in the direction of Mount Sara. When this action of routing the terrorist forces in Retimlje was carried out where the command of the 124th Brigade was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Whose 124th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's 124th Brigade of the KLA from the Operative Zone Pastrik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: These forces engaged in the blockade, do they go to cleanse the village, to clear the village?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blocking forces take up positions on one line. They do not engage in any manoeuvre, any movement. They have to stay on that line and, as required, to build fortifications on that line and to remain on the line until the assignment is completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number P1995. I hope that this document is not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, do you see the document before you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it yours?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a document of my brigade created after the execution of this action under the previous order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the second page in B/C/S, probably in English also is the second, count 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see the forces enumerated here, but we don't, or rather, is the logistical battalion here somewhere in these -- among these forces? Can you just take a brief look.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Move down in B/C/S; in English it's probably the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 7 in point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It begins with the words: "In the course of the third day of the b/d, the mopping-up operation of the remaining area around the village ..." Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Read the last sentence of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The forces under the blockade along the asphalt road and in the area of Siroko, Smac, and Donja Srbica were still in their positions."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What does that mean and do these forces include the battalion we mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That means that all the forces in the blockade in that section and in the section of the Prizren-Djakovica asphalt road who were performing the blockade kept standing in their places throughout all those days, as they had been ordered. That's why they are called the blocking forces, forces performing the blockade. They don't move.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number 20 -- P2015, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please read the heading and the date.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Joint Command for KiM, strictly confidential number 455-64, 23 March 1999, military secret, strictly confidential."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you used to receive such documents?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is the document that precedes the task. It's the document from the Pristina Corps, on the basis of which I wrote my own order, on the basis of which the mission was later accomplished.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: From whom did you receive this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like all the other documents from the superior command, I received it from the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How? How would you normally receive such documents, can you describe?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For as long as it was possible and practicable, and at this time it was still possible, messengers [Realtime transcript read in error "messages"] from my brigade would go to Pristina and would bring back military post in a special locked pouch. And all these orders were inside envelopes, properly sealed, with stamps affixed, and numbered.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We have error in transcript, Your Honour. Page 65, line 13. Not messages, but couriers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, they would have been messengers, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have Exhibit Number 5D1365, please. Could we have horizontal, please, and upper left corner a little bit bigger, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this the kind of envelope that you received such post? What is this?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. In the left corner we see the stamp of the military post.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But tell us, what is this.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a regular envelope in which documents and orders from the Pristina Corps were received.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you explain the stamp in the left upper corner? Whose stamp is it? What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the stamp of the Pristina Corps, that is, the military post of the Pristina Corps. We call it the rectangular stamp into which confidentiality indication is inscribed, the number of the document inside and the date when the document was created. On the other side they write whether it's delivered by courier or in some other way. In the bottom corner we see military post of the receiving brigade, that's my brigade, 549th Motorised. And this reference to Jablanica, that's a reference to a military activity that took place in the month of April in the broader area of Jablanica, and that's why this is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please read the number in the left upper corner on the stamp that you described.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Strictly confidential 455-115."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have P2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you read the strictly confidential number in the left upper corner.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Strictly confidential 455-115, dated 2nd April."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about Jablanica, is that the same number we saw on the envelope?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same number, and from the other numbers that I see this is the order that was inside the envelope because it's written in pencil that it's my brigade in the upper right corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it appropriate time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If this is a convenient time to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, it is not, but my colleagues are so upset. I would like to continue, but -- I would like to continue with your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Maybe five minutes or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay, just do that. I think that we have such a long break this time that that's in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have on our screens P2015, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before we move on to that, Mr. Delic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just the number is important -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- the Jablanica that's referred to here is in which municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jablanica, that's in Djakovica municipality, part of it; the other part is in Decani municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is it the only Jablanica in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see, General, the number and the date in the upper left corner. Read only that.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 455-63, dated 23rd March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number, again, P1995. First paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, would you read the first paragraph, please. It begins with the words: "In the period from 25th March until 29 March ..."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the period from 25 March until 29 March 1999, pursuant to the Order by the Commander of the 549th Motorised Brigade for providing the support to the MUP, Ministry of the Interior, forces and pursuant to the Order by the Pristina Corps, strictly confidential number 455-63 dated 23rd March 1999 ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, based on which document are you informing the Pristina Corps, is that the one we saw a moment ago or another one?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of that order, the previous one and my own order, I notified the command of the Pristina Corps of the accomplished task and I informed them how it was accomplished.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You read the number and the previous number and date. Are they the same?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same number, the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To whom was this analysis sent?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my command, the command of the Pristina Corps, that is, my superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, we saw in the heading that it says "Joint Command." It doesn't read "Pristina Corps." How did you understand the origin of that previous document, 455-63?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never any doubt in my mind, regardless of the reference to the Joint Command in the heading. I always knew that it was from my commander, that is, the command of the Pristina Corps, because concerning these tasks that were very extensive during my morning briefings to the commander and debriefings, I had previously received a verbal instruction from him that as soon as this task is handed down I should proceed to coordinate with the MUP and prepare my units for the execution of that task. So when I received the order I didn't really pay much attention to the heading at the top, this reference to the Joint Command, because it meant absolutely nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, we need to have a break again, this time until 2.15, and we will resume in a different courtroom, in Courtroom I. Please again would you leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.55 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, it's me again. General, Prosecution witnesses Isuf Zhuniqi and Sabri Popaj testified here and they claim that on the 25th of March, 1999, forces of the FRY and Serbia surrounded and attacked the village of Bela Crkva. I would be interested in the following: On that day, did your forces surround that village?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not correct. In military terminology when one says to encircle, to surround, that means to encircle a territory from all sides. The village of Bela Crkva was never encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your forces on that morning, did they have any activity in the village of Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that morning, sometime from 5.00 until 5.30, my forces went through the village of Bela Crkva towards the hill of Amovac. That was Combat Group 2 from my brigade. I, myself, went through Bela Crkva on that morning, also sometime between 5.00 and 6.00. I continued according to my plan through Bela Crkva, Orahovac, to the location that I decided would be my command post during these combat activities from the 25th until the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did a unit remain in the village?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Units of the second combat group, as they came in marching order, they came through the village of Crkva, Bela Crkva, from the west side, they went to the east side, to the foot of that hill, Amovac, from where they started taking up initial positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did they stop in the village itself? Did they have some activity in the village itself at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not have any activity in the village. I stayed very briefly just to see whether the units arrived according to plan and whether everything was all right. That's around 5.00. The village was peaceful. Truth to tell, I did not see any civilians, any civilian population; only the barking of dogs could be heard in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Prosecution witness Sabri Popaj claims that the army and police around the 18th of March, 1999, started digging trenches above the village at a distance of 1 kilometre and that that is where they placed two anti-aircraft guns or cannons. My question is whether the army did have positions above the village of Bela Crkva on the eve of the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not correct. There were no other troops there apart from my troops, and there was no need for any trenches to be dug and for some military positions to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The same witness alleges that on the morning of the 25th of March, 1999, five tanks passed by, out of which two tanks entered the school-yard, where they stayed until the 4th of May, 1999. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. Three tanks by which Combat Group 2 had been reinforced passed that morning through the village, just like other units, and they got out to the eastern rim of the village. Later on, when the unit set out, it set out just like the other part of the unit towards the village of -- towards the hill of Amovac. However, my units, my tanks, on those days never returned to that village again. Upon completing their activity on the 28th, they all returned to their own areas. So it is impossible for them to be, or rather, to have tanks or combat equipment there because no one else had tanks in that area except for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number 5D1332, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting for the map, witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- says that some villages used flame-throwers in the village. My question is whether the Army of Yugoslavia had flame-throwers at all?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the Second World War up until 1955 or 1956, there were flame-throwers but they were taken out of all units, they were decommissioned, and they haven't been in the military for a long, long time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The witness concerned is Isuf Zhuniqi; it was his claim, his allegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll -- could we zoom in, please, central part. Zoom out, please. A little bit up, scroll up, up, up, sorry, opposite direction. That's fine, and could you zoom in now. Upper part, if it's possible to zoom in, a little bit left, down -- down, down, please, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, could you just give us instructions as to how it would be easiest for us to find Bela Crkva and Celine on this map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to move it to the left. The other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Right-hand side, please, right-hand side, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now a bit up --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see it here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could you zoom in the part of the map where we have the numbers 549, please. Upper right corner -- actually, upper left corner. A little bit down. Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, can you find your way on this map or should we use another map?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can find my way, that's no problem. I know this territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you see where the village of Bela Crkva is?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have electronic pen, please, for General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you first tell me what your task was on that morning, why were your forces on the move?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are documents through which we already went. The task of the brigade was, in coordination with MUP forces, to block the terrorist forces, primarily referring to the 124th Brigade of the KLA from Operation Zone Pastrik that was in the area of Suva Reka, Orahovac, Prizren. However, the blockade should be along the line of the road from the village of Pirane, to the village of Rogovo, and on the other side, including Gornja Srbica, Donja Srbica, in that general direction. As for the other forces from the area of Suva Reka, part of them, rather, from the area of Orahovac, they should be linked up and the terrorist forces should be encircled, the terrorist forces that were in the area of Retimlje where the command of the 124th Brigade was in the first place. I can mark these locations where they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you think is best for me, how should I mark Bela Crkva? Just as a dot?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just move -- just draw the axis of how your unit was moving and describe for us its further movement.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for its further movement, since part of Combat Group 2 from the area of the winery, the wine cellar, also went up to the hill called Amovac, on this line they were to take up initial positions, and from these positions they were to go out to attack Retimlje. Am I to draw that direction, that axis too?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please and draw a circle around Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction of the attack -- well, this pen doesn't really work very well, does it? That's for Combat Group 2. It went through Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, where was there the first armed conflict with the KLA forces?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA forces -- well, the first clash was in the village of Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's the same colour, otherwise we use different colours to mark things.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the blue pen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village of Celine, the village of Brestovac, and the village of Nogavac, it's along this axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Right. We're interested in that axis now. You said that you went through the village of Bela Crkva, that there was no activity there, and you marked the village of Celine for us. Prosecution witnesses appeared Agim Jemini and Reshit Salihi, and they claim that the forces of the FRY and Serbia on that day, the 25th [Realtime transcript read error "24th"] of March, 1999, surrounded the village of Celine with tanks and armoured personnel carriers. Could you please tell me, did you have armoured personnel carriers in your units?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- when my learned friend is making reference to prior allegations of the Prosecution witnesses, if I could have a specific reference, either to a paragraph in their statement or a line in the transcript because I want to verify that the way it's being read out is accurately reflecting exactly how those witnesses phrased it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, can you do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I will try to do my best to give the reference during this session. I read the transcripts and the statements, which are in system, because all those witnesses are -- they were testified under the Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The reference to the statement would also satisfy Mr. Hannis, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I mean, the phrase sometimes used "surrounded the village," that may not be the way the witness testified but that's the question the witness is answering and it's not meeting head-on is my concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'll clarify that in very short period of time. May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They state that the village of Celine on that morning was surrounded, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the reference --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- did your forces --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have the reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we have the reference for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If we have just one minute, please, I'll give you the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I just received information that there are plenty of technical problems right now also look as Defence team has got that problem, my assistant. I hope Mr. Visnjic has got --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Agim Jemini transcript in the Milosevic case, P525353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That will be T, I think, rather than P and there must be one number too many in that. It was a long trial but not that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, it's a Prosecution exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I can assist. Prosecution Exhibit 52338 is the statement of Agim Jemini, paragraph 2, 4, and 3 of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're drowning in a sea of references yet, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I know our exhibits haven't reached the 50.000 level yet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the first one is 5353, I think -- sorry, 2353.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe that number's too high for a witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the reference that I gave was 52338, or rather, P2338.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Still too high, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: 2338 seems to be a reference to that witness's transcript in Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, that's his statement. I'm sorry. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you can continue with the question now, Mr. Cepic, because it doesn't actually depend on the particular word that's in issue here. What you want to know is whether there were any personnel carriers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did you have within your troops armoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I had a motorised unit, we did not have any APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, on that morning did your forces surround the village of Celine?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The forces did not surround the village of Celine. The forces were on the south-west side near the railway and the asphalt road leading from Prizren to Zrze.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Witness Jemini said that that settlement was shelled on that day. Did your forces perhaps shell the village of Celine?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces did not shell the village of Celine. The support that was given, the fire support that was given, was above the village of Celine along the elevations where the trenches of terrorists were located. So referring to the light artillery, I think those were 130-millimetre guns. Fire was directed above the village, not affecting the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark where the trenches were. Could you draw that in.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's pretty difficult to do that, to draw that in. I'm trying to draw one thing and something else comes up on the screen. Above the village, towards the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Please tell me, was the village of Celine organized for combat and was there any combat there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first fire contact was in the village of Celine and it was a police unit that had it. I think it was at around 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me, General, did your forces pass through the village?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the police unit neutralised the terrorist forces in the village, the activities continued on towards the village of Velika Krusa and Ram Dubrava, along that axis. The forces that were at Amovac continued activities towards Nogavac, Brestovac, and Mala Hoca, thus part of my forces which came from the direction of Bela Crkva sometime at around 10.00 passed after the police along their axis through the village of Celine along the road leading from Bela Crkva towards Celine. Following that, a mortar platoon, 120-millimetre mortars, passed through. They did not open fire from the sector of Bela Crkva because there was no need for that. They moved to a different firing position, which was to the east of the village of Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did your forces remain in Celine?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not have such task. They continued on along the axis Nogavac-Brestovac-Mala Hoca, towards Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the date that this occurred, Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 25th of March, all of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, the evidence I think we're dealing with is about the 24th of March. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think 25th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Of March. So there's --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: March --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- is there an error then of the transcript at page 6, line 12?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yeah, this is an error. It has to be 25th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, Witness Agim Jemini stated that members of the army entered the village in lines of four soldiers and that they surrounded the village from 9.30 to 10.00 in this manner and that there were 500 soldiers coming from all directions. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. It is very strange to say that the soldiers came in in lines of four. They did not attend a parade. They were in a combat march and there was no need for them to surround the village anymore after this combat contact with police, which lasted for about one hour and 40 minutes, following which the police took the village. So that my forces which came from Bela Crkva to the village after the police forces simply passed through the village. There was no longer any resistance in the village because the terrorists had withdrawn along the axis from Celine towards Ram Dubrava and Donje Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please draw in the movement of BG-2, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We heard from the said witness that the army remained in the village for another two days.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. The army did not stay on. They passed through Bela Crkva, and following that they passed partially through Celine and partially through Brestovac, Nogavac, and then they continued towards the task, towards the general goal, which was Retimlje. We have simply been following BG-2 here, and during that time other units moved along their own axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that as well. We need to cover the village of Celine first. Did your forces perhaps loot or destroy property and destroy the old village in Celine on that day as they passed through?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only active-duty soldiers participated in this activity because there were no members who had been mobilised. Active-duty soldiers do not loot. What could they loot when such soldiers only carry their back-packs on their backs, and those back-packs can only carry a lunch, some bandages, 150 bullets of a combat set, and perhaps one or two hand-grenades. That's all that they can fit into their back-pack or rucksack. So I don't see what could they have possibly looted and carry with them. Ultimately, they had their superiors accompanying them and it was their duty [as interpreted] to prevent such conduct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you moved, were you on roads or were you on countryside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're referring to Bela Crkva, we had come along the asphalt group [as interpreted]. The combat group had moved from Djakovica across Zrze along the asphalt road towards Bela Crkva. Following that, they took the macadam road through Bela Crkva towards the eastern border of Bela Crkva. After that the unit did not move along roads, they moved along the manoeuvre terrain. They crossed the creek running along Nogavac, Brestovac, and Mala Hoca wherever it was possible. I'm here referring to the combat equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I think that we have a small error in transcript, page 12, lines 22 and 23, I think actually in line 23 we missed the word -- he said: "It was their duty and order to prevent such conduct."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, now that we're dealing with the village of Celine, I have just one question pertaining to the time when the OSCE mission was on the ground. Did you have a check-point nearby the village of Celine during the OSCE mission?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not only did -- not only we didn't have any check-point, nobody else did. We were not allowed to do that because we were within the border belt. The police also had a limited number of observation points and there were absolutely no observation points along this road or in any of the settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was that territory under the control of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From January, February, and onwards, through March, the number of problems in that territory was on the increase. I have already said so and you can see it in one of the documents. We have already examined that the territory of Suva Reka, Orahovac, and Velika Krusa increasingly came under the control of terrorists. And already in February the road leading from Suva Reka across Studencane towards Orahovac was closed. One couldn't use that road except when the OSCE mission escorted police patrols. The other road was open, that is, the road between Prizren and Djakovica; however, there had been attacks along that road on individual vehicles, MUP vehicles, MUP patrols. As for my unit, since I didn't move along that road, I used other roads for the border belt, there had been no attacks on my units in that area. It was particularly frequent in the area of Pirane.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did your soldiers perhaps wear black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All soldiers of my brigade wore prescribed uniforms, M-89; as for military police, they had uniforms M-94. Those are camouflage uniforms, greenish in colour, that are establishment uniforms in the army. Nobody wore black uniforms because such uniforms did not exist in the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did your soldiers wear Tito-style caps?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were put out of use a long time ago. All soldiers wore berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, did your soldiers wear bands around their heads in that area?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand, what would those bands signify? They would signify lack of discipline and soldiers did not wear such bands around their heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You have already mentioned that while carrying out that assignment, that task, you had no reservists among your forces. Witness Agim Jemini claimed that he recognised some soldiers from Orahovac who were between 30 and 40 years old. Were there any military units in Orahovac and did you have any soldiers of that age carrying out that assignment?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were never any troops in Orahovac. There is no garrison there, no barracks. And as for the age of the soldiers, my soldiers were between 20 and 21 years old, those were conscripts serving their military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. General, could you please show you us the axes of movement of other units in the implementation of these -- this task, and could you indicate to us whether your forces -- the 25th, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Orahovac --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Your Honour, with your leave, is it technically possible to have an IC number for this first map, actually drawing, and later on to keep the same drawing and to add something more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can give it an IC number and then when you want to add to it, you call up the IC number and not the original exhibit number. So you wish a number now, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, if it's possible to have IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be IC150, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, could you indicate to us the axis of movement of the second unit of your composition that was moving towards Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat Group 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you want it back on the screen now, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I think that's what you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we have a third colour --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If we could see IC150, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, can you indicate it to us now.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat Group 6 moved from the direction of Orahovac. This colour now is quite different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's the idea. You're going to get the full-coloured pencil set.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Combat Group 7 moved along this road, along the road towards Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm now interested in Velika Krusa and Mala Krusa. I'd like to put a few questions to you in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along that axis, my Combat Group 1 from the asphalt road, that is to say, including Pirane and to the cellar in Mala Krusa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, Suva Reka is towards the right-hand side of this and you've put some black markings on the map. Are we talking about those at the top those or those at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cepic asked just now that I show my forces that were in the area of Pirane and Mala Krusa. On the side of Suva Reka, there were my forces as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm now lost on what the black represents, Mr. Cepic, or which road we're talking about towards Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think we'll spend a lot of time if we continue in this way, so I will try to focus just on the main things and to clarify in relation to those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, let's just go back to the location of Mala Krusa, Velika Krusa. You just said now that the disposition of forces was from the village of Pirane to the wine cellar. Could you please tell me --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are forces of my Combat Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your forces, that is, the 25th of March, 1999, did they enter the villages themselves of Mala Krusa and Velika Krusa?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My forces did not enter these villages because these villages were not on the axis of my forces. Part of my forces were from the 25th to the 27th all the time on the asphalt road from Pirane to up near Rogovo. But as for passing through these villages, that had to do with a MUP unit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now we would be interested in the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second. We haven't got the end of that answer. You said: "But as for passing through these villages, that had to do with a MUP unit," and did you say a little more than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that through Velika Krusa and Mala Krusa, along their axis, towards Ram Dubrava, MUP units passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was any fire opened from that direction of Velika Krusa at the forces?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Velika Krusa, in Mala Krusa, like in Celine, fire was opened at our forces, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark with a blue pen from where these -- the position that these forces were firing from.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I haven't practiced this enough, but it's very hard to do this. This is roughly where these blue lines are. That is the upper half of both villages, that is where the firing at the police came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, on the 25th of March, Combat Group 1, 25th of March, 1999, did Combat Group 1 keep its positions there or did it move on?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat Group 1, on the 25th of March, entered the village of Pirane, and from the village of Pirane it was supposed to go towards the village of Medvedce and Zojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that for us.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just underline these villages? The village of Zojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now let us briefly deal with the village of Pirane. Prosecution witness Rahim Latifi testified here and he said on that morning, the 25th of March, the forces of Serbia surrounded that village with tanks and different vehicles and that then there was shelling. Could you tell us what actually happened on that morning in Pirane on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village was not surrounded. The forces of the army were on the road, and from the asphalt road they set up combat order and they moved in this direction, partly towards Zojic and Medvedce and partly towards Ram Dubrava. There was no firing from the first houses, but as for the houses that are on the northern rim of the village, fire was opened at the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark this with blue.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no shelling of the village. The village had not been surrounded, because if the army was only on its south-western side the village was free, so to speak, towards Istok -- towards the east, towards the west, and the units were moving along the following direction: South-west/north-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that for us.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's already marked here. There is an arrow showing that, showing the direction of activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was this village a KLA stronghold?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this village was a KLA stronghold in the earlier period and in the later period. There was a lot of firing from that village at the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The road where you marked your forces, what road is that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Prizren-Djakovica road. It's a main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me whether on that occasion your forces destroyed the mosque in Pirane.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mosque in Pirane was not destroyed during these initial activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me whether your unit remained in these positions on that day or did it go on further north?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the course of that day, the unit had reached the vineyards that were above the village, towards Ram Dubrava; however, because it was an open area and because of the fire that was coming from Ram Dubrava and Medvedce, perhaps a few hundred metres away from the village, that is where it spent that night, between the 25th and the 26th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that for us on the map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you place number 1 there at the location where your forces spent the night.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Have you placed a number there, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, we cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I mark the number in a different colour then?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, use the same colour.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you. General, up until the 26th, Combat Group 2 and the other forces that went to Retimlje, how far did they get? Where did they stop during the night between the 25th and the 26th?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they come across any resistance from the terrorist forces there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although in this direction where parts of this combat group were, towards the village of Brestovac, there was less firing and less resistance. The resistance was further down south along the axis of those units that were moving towards Ram Dubrava and Donje Retimlje; however, that would roughly be the line where they were on the second day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, what was the mark for where they stopped? How is it marked so we can reflect it in the record?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, could you please put a number 2 at the location where your forces stopped.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would be interested in the following. General, on the 25th, in the evening, did you go through Velika Krusa?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went through part of Velika Krusa. I went through part of Nogavac and Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you spend any time there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not stay there longer than necessary. I think it was around 1900 hours in the evening that I came from the area of Orahovac via the hill of Amovac, then I entered Nogavac here, then got to Velika Hoca -- no, Velika Krusa, where I met up with one of the commanders of the police unit that had a problem here. One of my vehicles went with me, a tank, because here in the area of the village of Nogavac this BOV-3 of the police had tipped over and they could not get it out of the river. And during the course of the day, I ordered a tank of mine to come from Prizren and to wait for me at the exit from Orahovac and Velika Hoca. It was already dark, so I got it there and I went together with this commander to see where the BOV that had tipped over was. That is where I issued an order to this officer of mine. I was still in that area around 2000 hours when they told me that my barracks at Prizren had been bombed; namely, the building of the police. When I issued that order, ordering that task, I got out of the asphalt road here and went to Prizren to my barracks, where I saw what the building looked like, the one that had been bombed around 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, page 22, line 13, the witness said [B/C/S spoken] but in transcript we have just the tank.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Recovery tank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you explained to us the disposition of forces was on the 25th, you told us what the initial positions were on the 26th, you explained where the blocking forces were situated. Did you by any chance hear that on the 26th of March, 1999, in Mala Krusa 105 Albanians had been killed. Did you have this information at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I had not heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And had you heard something like that, what measures would you have taken?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my unit is concerned, it is quite well-known what the measures would have been. It would be impossible to do something of the sort if any officers were around; but had I heard that anyone had done something like that, I would have taken the following measures. I would have arrested my personnel immediately and sent them to the military court. If I had heard that somebody else had done something like that, for instance, a MUP unit, I would immediately have informed the chief of the secretariat because he was the highest-ranking police officer in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Some clarification, Mr. Delic. You said that the barracks at Prizren were bombed and you referred to these as being the barracks of the police, the building of the police. Do you mean a MUP building or do you mean the military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in some of the barracks in Kosovo and Metohija, because of some problems that dated from the 1980s, there would be a building in one such -- in each barracks of that kind that belonged to the police, not the military police, but the regular police; so in Prizren, Djakovica, Pec, and I think in Pristina too, there was a building, a police building, within our barracks. This building that was targeted by three missiles, it was a police building, three police officers were killed, and two were wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The other point of clarification I would like is: When did you learn about the murder of the 105 Albanians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as this is concerned, I can't really tell you now specifically when the indictment was made public and when we learned from our subordinate -- from our superiors.
