I know that General Pavkovic called the officers from Kosovo and Metohija to report. I was asked specifically about this area because I was the commander. He asked me what I knew about that and whether my unit had done that, and then we were given an order to write a statement about what we knew about those events that were made public in the indictment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I just want to know when you discovered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And on the 2 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was the year 2000, not 2001. I think it was 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And where were you on the 26th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 26th of March, 1999? Well, I can show you the exact spot where I was on the 25th and on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you had got back to Prizren on the evening of the 25th. Were you back in the area on the map on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, I went back to the same spot on the 26th to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How close were you to Mala Krusa on the 26th, at any time on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was about 5 to 6 kilometres away from Mala Krusa. I was on the opposite direction on the Orahovac-Suva Reka road at Krasta feature, where I had decided that my command post should be, and I was accompanied by the deputy commander of the 37th Police Detachment, Major Grujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have an IC number for this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC151, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you said that you heard about this incident at Mala and Velika Krusa. Do you know if anyone was ever convicted for this incident? Did you hear anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear that because at the same time the president of the municipality of Orahovac was convicted and another man, I think his last name is Jovanovic or Blagojevic. They were tried in Prizren before a regular court, and this man was tried for the crimes committed in Bela Crkva, Celine, Mala Krusa, Velika Krusa for the deportations, rapes, everything that was in the indictment he was charged with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think his last name is Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, were there any situations in your unit where civilians would be killed or where there would be other violations of international humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were such situations in my unit too, in the period that followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were any of these crimes prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three cases. We learned about two of these at the moment when they happened, one involved a soldier who killed a civilian, it was a military police officer. He was arrested by the military police and was handed over to the war court. The other situation involved an officer who also committed a crime, it was a captain by the name of Vujadin Stekovic. He was also arrested and was sent to face the war court in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, we learned about yet another crime that was allegedly committed by two soldiers and two officers; they were also prosecuted before the military court in Nis.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What were these crimes? You've told us the first one was murder but what were the other two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All three crimes were murders of civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How many civilians were killed in those incidents?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven civilians were killed, and in 1998, since it says in all my records that eight civilians were killed, in 1998 another Albanian civilian was killed or died, but it was in the course of a night-time engagement with the terrorists and he was on the opposite side but he came out to the terrace of his house and he switched on the light and the unit that had been under attack opened fire and killed him. But we dealt with that incident with his parents, we talked to his parents and the people from the village, and they came to realize that this was not done on purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is an extra one over and above the other three, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, but it is not a war crime. The three instances happened during the war, the ones that I mentioned, but this one was before the war, in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, are you going to be presenting any formal records of these prosecutions?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For all three of the prosecutions?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Actually, I haven't got documents from the court, but I have the exhibit which is P962. This exhibit is from the brigade -- actually, 549th Brigade about all criminal records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, often these don't tell us what happened in the cases. In this instance do we know what actually happened, whether there were convictions and sentences?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We've got some informations in relation to that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And also this document reflected some information about the judgements and the further procedure in those cases. May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you wanting that on the screen or are you continuing with something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave, a little bit later just to finish the crime base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, were your forces in the village of Nogavac itself from the 25th until the 28th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My forces only passed through the village of Nogavac. They stayed only for as long as it was necessary to go on, so maybe 10 to 15 minutes, and in this period or, in fact, even after this period they never came back to that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did your forces have any contact and did they surround 8.000 people around -- close to the village of Nogavac and order them to leave that area on the 26th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of any instance where 8.000 people would be gathered in a single place except in statements, and this I talked about in 2005. The commander of the 2nd Battalion, who was also the commander of Combat Group 2 at that time, reported that there was a group of about 200 people, women and children, who were there, close to the village of Nogavac. I don't know whether it was in Brzina or in Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. And on the 28th of March, did your forces by any chance force the people to get out of the woods there - we're now talking about the village of Celine - took their ID documents and forced them to walk to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said on the 28th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 28th of March, that's the village of Celine.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th of March my units were not there at all. They were in an area completely away from Celine. Combat Group 2 was in the area of the village of Mamusa and Combat Group 5 was in the vicinity of the village of Dobrodeljane, and by the 28th of March all the other combat groups had already come back to their positions and started launching attacks in the direction of Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. On the 2nd of April, 1999, as alleged by Witness Isuf Zhuniqi, an air bomb was dropped from Yugoslav air force aeroplane on the village of Nogavac. Is that possible at all, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not possible because our air force was not flying in the air-space above the whole of the state, and particularly not above Kosovo and Metohija. The aircraft, the air force, the aeroplanes that were up at the beginning of the war were mostly active in the skies above Belgrade, but then they were mostly destroyed, but those were fighter planes carrying missiles designed to engage enemy aircraft. Our aircraft did not carry bombs. At that time it was impossible for our planes to take off, given that NATO had absolute supremacy in the air-space.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we already saw the video clip. My learned friend Mr. Visnjic played for us, 3D710. And my learned friend Hannis objected about that exhibit because he explained that General Smiljanic wasn't there in Nogavac on 2nd April of 1999. So with your leave, I would like to play this short video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if -- I'm not sure if this General was here and seeing it he can tell us that, but I don't know that we need to show it to him first. If he was there, he can tell us that and then maybe we can play the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How about that, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Actually, we have another exhibit number, it is the same material but different exhibit number. And I will ask -- before we play --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- I will ask the witness to clarify this situation and about this video. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, in proofing I showed you this video clip, Nogavac, the 2nd of April, 1999. Can you tell us something more about this event. What is this all about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early in the morning on the 2nd of April, NATO aviation bombed the village -- the houses in the village of Nogavac. A number of houses were destroyed, a lot of civilians were killed, those who were wounded were treated by us in the Prizren hospital. On the following day, the Ministry of the Interior Prizren SUP carried out an on-site investigation and established the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us something about the origin of the clip that I showed you during proofing.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a clip of the Radio Television Serbia, the Prizren studio.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who produced this clip, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I remember that there was Borivoje Ugrinovic on the spot, he was in charge of that studio incidentally. There was also a cameraman there, as far as I remember, that was somebody called Sakotic; he works in the Belgrade studio of Radio Television Serbia nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were you in Nogavac yourself on that morning?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I learned of it later. I talked to the chief of the secretariat. I was shown this clip, this footage. Since we asked that every location that was bombed in those first days be recorded on video camera or if this was in the -- in the border belt, we asked that it be done by our people and in locations elsewhere it was done by the people from the studio in Prizren, the studio of Radio Television Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was it you were told about the filming that had been done and shown it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was -- it happened on the 2nd in the morning and it was filmed that very day, probably at around noon, midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was it shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw it on the same day, sometime in the afternoon or in the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Carry on then, Mr. Visnjic -- Mr. Cepic, if you want to show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we play this video, please, 5D1242, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, this woman in the clip talking in the hospital, what language did she speak in?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Siptar language.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were the wounded treated?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of those wounded were hospitalised and treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We saw remains of a bomb. Did you have any additional information about it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The remains of this missile that you saw, it wasn't that missile that produced all that damage on the houses. There were a lot of such missiles in my territory. These are anti-radar missiles, HAR. As for the bombs that were dropped, we couldn't see their remains or traces except for stabilizer fins. At the time, the bombs most often used were MK-82, bombs that are about 225 kilos in weight, typical ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who would be responsible for firing the missile we could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are NATO missiles, NATO equipment. I don't know from which country the planes that dropped the bombs originated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the bomb. The anti-radar missile, was that a NATO missile?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Those are missiles which, if it is detected, or if it is believed, they react to infrared radiation. It is sufficient to have a fire on the ground or sometimes it is sufficient for an engine of a car, of a truck to be on for them to detect it. And when they detect it, they fire the missiles and the missiles are built in on the planes in such a way that sometimes they are launched without the pilot doing anything if they detect any radar activity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, the first word of your answer was enough for the question. You appreciate that. It's a simple question, let's have simple answers, we're simple-minded people. Please proceed, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, do you know where the village is Dusanovo is located?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The village of Dusanovo used to be and nowadays still is a suburb of Prizren. It is linked to Prizren and one cannot see where Dusanovo ends and Prizren begins nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've now lost me completely. I thought we were talking about Nogavac. Have we moved from that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought you were challenging the evidence of Isuf Zhuniqi and that seemed very important, but we're talking about a different area being bombed, are we, from the one that he claimed he saw Serb fighters -- Yugoslav fighters dealing with?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, are we? Are we dealing with something different?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is something different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I've lost the way somewhere. Sorry. It must be a lapse of concentration.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I just -- I just started the new topic related to village Dusanovo in the suburb of Prizren because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, so that's separate. The film we saw was of where? Nogavac?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Nogavac village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's fine. I haven't lost --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, I haven't lost the place. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, probably I made confusion. This video, as I said, is related to village of Nogavac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, now let us return to the village of Dusanovo; you said it was a suburb of Prizren. Tell me, please, in the beginning of the war, in late March, were your forces, or rather, your tanks in that settlement?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what I said previously, you could see that my tanks were deployed from the 25th until the 27th or 28th inclusive in that area. And following that, they were deployed in Malisevo. In Prizren, in the sector of an agricultural estate Landovica, I had two tanks that were out of order, so there was no way my tanks could have been in Dusanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please explain whether you had a tank in Dusanovo.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single tank of mine was in Dusanovo; however, I had two tanks in the sector of an agricultural estate Landovica, which is some 2 kilometres from Dusanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were those functioning, operational, tanks?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those tanks were out of order when it comes to combat use, but they were functioning in the sense that they were operational. They could not be used in combat because their aim mechanisms were at the time being repaired in Cacak, [indiscernible] equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, in late March of 1999, did your forces by any chance conduct a search operation in the village of Dusanovo?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no need to conduct such a search operation in that village and no unit of mine was issued with such a task. My units were located either in a border belt and then some units that we mentioned earlier were in the area towards Malisevo. Upon return from Malisevo, all units were deployed in the border belt defending the state border until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, Krasniqi Rexhep in his testimony in the second paragraph of his statement said that in the factory where he worked which was called Pretext [phoen] in Prizren - I'm quoting - there was no less than 50 tanks concealed and artillery pieces of 105-millimetres. This is what he said in his statement. Could this be true?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this cannot be true because I had a total of 31 combat tanks, out of which two were out of order, as I have told you, and were located in that sector throughout that entire period. There was another tank or two being repaired in Cacak at the time, and not a single tank of mine ever entered the compound of that factory called Perlunka [phoen]. As for the artillery, my unit never had these howitzers of 105 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. There's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was the evidence of Rexhep that the 50 included the artillery pieces or it was 50 tanks plus artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If you have just one minute, please, Your Honour, just to find the statement, second paragraph in statement. I've just received information from my learned friend Mr. Zecevic and he told me that 50 tanks plus artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, that same witness said that on the 28th of March, 1999, he saw 50 to 60 tanks in Dusanovo. I would like to know in the area of Prizren and the surrounding area, was there another unit? Was there another military formation there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, neither before the war or during the war was there any other unit except for my unit which had tanks. I have already told you how many tanks I had, and I have also told you what tasks those tanks implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just a reference for transcript, exhibit number for the statement, witness statement, of Mr. Krasniqi Rexhep is P2378.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, Suva Reka, on the 25th of March in the morning, did your forces surround the settlement of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not surround Suva Reka. I don't see the point of that. My forces passed through sometime between 4.00 until 4.30, they passed through Suva Reka until they reached the wine cellar of Metohija Vino or bus station, and then they continued on towards the village of Rastane, that village is located to the west of Suva Reka and is almost linked to Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were there any units of the Army of Yugoslavia in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no garrison in Suva Reka and there have never been any army units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, we have heard here in the courtroom some claims that mosques in Suva Reka, Celine, Rogovo, Bela Crkva, Brestovac, Velika Krusa, Vlastica, Landovica, and Djakovica were destroyed. Did your forces destroy any of these mosques?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my forces opened fire at the mosque in Landovica; as for other mosques, the answer is no. This instance when they opened fire took place on the 26th of March; however, the mosque was not destroyed, rather, just the minaret from which they had opened fire on the army. On that day in Landovica two soldiers were killed, one soldier was wounded, and we had to pull out the wounded soldier to treat him and we also had to retrieve the bodies of the dead soldiers. It wasn't possible to do that due to the fire that was opened from the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you can find a suitable place to interrupt, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think that is right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Delic, that's all we can do for today and also all we can do for this week, and it will be Tuesday before we resume, so you will have to come back then to continue your evidence. That will be at 2.15 on Tuesday, unless between now and then something changes and we can revert to the morning, but the arrangement is 2.15. So please be back in time to take up your evidence again, then, on Tuesday. Meanwhile, as you know the drill, you've been here before, it's vital to have no any communication with anyone, no matter what position they have, connection with you, whatever, about the evidence in the case. You must keep off that subject completely and deal with other things. Now could you please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you at 2.15 on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of December, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.00 p.m.,
